genes.text: Canonical formulation: `construct` returns the candidate directly in the verifier's own format.

Search a reflection-symmetric population containing three circles centred on the symmetry axis and nine mirrored pairs. Encode each pair by one centre and radius. Generate independent row arrangements and radius assignments, retain geometrically diverse elites, and periodically release symmetry before full constrained refinement.

Perform coordinated contact surgery: identify near-active circle and wall contacts, select connected clusters of three to six contacts, and temporarily permit violations only within each selected cluster. Apply a displacement targeting those contacts, restore all constraints by continuation, and retain distinct feasible contact graphs rather than only immediate score improvements.

Use destroy-and-repair moves that remove two to four spatially adjacent circles. Relax the surviving packing, then reinsert the removed circles into different voids using multiple starting radii and centres. Refine all 21 circles jointly and archive the best result from each distinct contact graph.

Generate alternative 21-circle families through neighbouring circle counts. Optimize 20-circle packings, insert a small circle into each promising void, and refine. Separately optimize 22-circle packings, delete each of several small or highly constrained circles, and refine the remaining 21. Enforce positive radii throughout the final optimization.

Trace aspect-ratio branches instead of optimizing box shape immediately. Fix width plus height to two, solve at a grid of width-to-height ratios from 0.4 to 2.5, and warm-start neighbouring ratios in both directions. Release the aspect ratio only after collecting local optima from different branches.

Implement sequential inner-approximation LPs over centres, radii, and box dimensions. For each pair, freeze its current unit separation vector and impose that the projected new separation exceeds the sum of radii. Maximize total radius subject to linear wall constraints and a centre trust region; update directions after every accepted step.

Use fixed-centre radius LP dual multipliers to build a local model for moving centres. Weight pair-distance derivatives and wall terms by their dual sensitivities, propose a trust-region step, then resolve the radius LP to measure actual improvement. Reject inaccurate predictions and reduce the trust radius near LP basis changes.

Polish promising packings with an explicit constrained solver using analytic derivatives, rather than ending with a penalty objective. Optimize centres, positive radii, and box width with height equal to two minus width. Enforce every squared-distance and wall inequality, then independently validate the resulting unsquared float distances and exact-Fraction perimeter.

Seed searches from mixed-radius lattice families rather than only jittered rectangular grids. Enumerate staggered row-count compositions totalling 21, initialize two or three radius classes, and place smaller circles in inter-row or boundary gaps. Optimize each construction first within its row ordering, then release all ordering constraints.

Replace blanket radius shrinkage with minimum-loss feasibility repair. Recompute pair distances using the verifier's exact floating-point expression, impose conservative pair bounds in a radius LP, and reserve a tiny perimeter margin. Recheck exact Fractions and adjust offending radii with nextafter until valid; measure score loss separately from geometric optimization.

Optimize an enclosing rectangle's width jointly with disk centers and radii, using direct smooth separation inequalities and linear wall inequalities. The returned object stores centers and radii separately, plus descriptive box dimensions; the adapter assembles the frozen circle triples without any floating-point transformations.

Optimize all circle centres, radii, and rectangle width jointly using explicit nonlinear non-overlap inequalities and linear wall constraints, rather than a sequence of squared-violation penalties. Supply analytic objective and constraint derivatives so the constrained optimizer can refine dense contact configurations accurately.

Use multiple structured starts: refine a valid incumbent, try staggered near-hexagonal row layouts with different row populations, then restart from perturbed centres of the best verified packing. Preserve the best candidate under the exact verifier so unsuccessful or numerically infeasible restarts cannot degrade the result.

Optimize centres, radii, and rectangle width using successive linear programs whose circle-pair constraints are supporting separation half-planes. Refresh those planes after each solve, then polish the original distance constraints. The serialized representation remains canonical circles, so adaptation is the identity.

Represent a horizontally reflection-symmetric packing by twelve circle orbits: three axis circles and nine mirrored pairs. Optimize orbit coordinates, radii, and rectangle width; periodically require several near-contact orbit pairs to separate before restoring the original objective. The adapter expands each orbit into canonical circles, while canonical incumbents remain valid passthrough objects.

Optimize Cartesian centers, radii, and rectangle width with analytic non-overlap constraints. Use a reflection-reduced initialization, then remove all orbit equalities for unrestricted polishing. Candidates store separate center and radius arrays; canonical incumbents pass through unchanged.

Seed reflection-symmetric searches with a staggered triangular-lattice construction: three axis circles, four mirrored pairs in an inner row, and five in an outer row. Project an incumbent into this symmetry only when its score is competitive; avoid forcing poor cold starts into an unsuitable orbit assignment.

Repair each candidate by shrinking radii enough to eliminate all overlaps, then recenter and uniformly rescale the entire packing to saturate the bounding-box width-plus-height constraint, allowing expansion as well as contraction. Apply a small floating-point safety margin and retain candidates only after checking the exact verifier.

Diversify starts by construction topology rather than only perturbing an incumbent’s contacts. For a reflection-symmetric packing, build several arrangements with different populations in the off-axis rows, expand each into mirrored pairs plus axis singles, and locally optimize each alongside the incumbent-derived start.

Repair candidate overlaps by uniformly shrinking radii using the minimum pairwise distance-to-radius-sum ratio, then rescale the entire packing to saturate the bounding-box width-plus-height limit—even when this enlarges it. Leave small floating-point safety margins and accept improvements only after checking the exact verifier.

Partition the search budget into independently time-limited local optimizations rather than repeatedly forcing selected contacts apart. Save the latest iterate during each solve so interruption preserves a restart point, and maintain a separate best candidate after feasibility repair and exact verification.

Give each local optimization a wall-clock slice within the global budget, rather than relying only on iteration limits. Save callback iterates frequently; when a slice expires, repair and verify the latest iterate, then continue the search. This prevents one expensive solve from monopolizing the budget while preserving partial progress.

Maintain an archive indexed by contact graph and aspect-ratio bin. Reserve parent slots for distinct feasible graphs even when their scores are below the incumbent. Cross parents by transplanting a spatial cluster of two to four circles, repair the interface, and jointly refine; reject duplicate graphs rather than merely duplicate coordinates.

Trace packing branches with rectangle width fixed and height equal to two minus width. Sweep width in both directions from several structurally distinct starts, warm-start each branch, and retain hysteresis or contact-graph changes. Release width only after the sweep, then refine and verify each distinct branch.

Test coordinated contact surgery on connected clusters of three to six active contacts, including mirrored clusters when symmetry is imposed. Drive the selected gaps through a finite continuation excursion before restoring feasibility. Archive distinct repaired contact graphs despite temporary score loss, and periodically release symmetry for unrestricted refinement.

Use a time-sliced portfolio of structurally different starts rather than polishing only the incumbent. Include symmetry projections and distinct lattice constructions, rank their optimized results using objective minus an infeasibility penalty, and preserve verifier-valid improvements throughout each solve so unfinished runs still contribute.

Alternate collective coordinate jitter with coordinated contact perturbations. Perturb all symmetry-reduced center coordinates while keeping mirrored copies linked; periodically instead impose positive gaps on several near-contact pairs. Restore the original constraints and locally optimize after either move, retaining only verified improvements.

Repair each candidate by shrinking radii enough to remove all pairwise overlaps, then uniformly rescale centres and radii to use the full width-plus-height budget—even when this enlarges the configuration. Apply tiny inward safety factors and validate with the exact verifier before retaining improvements.

Give each local optimization a wall-clock slice rather than relying only on iteration limits. Preserve its latest iterate on interruption and periodically validate intermediate candidates, so one difficult solve cannot consume the entire search budget or discard useful progress.

Trace finite contact-surgery branches instead of immediately restoring the incumbent objective. Select connected clusters of three to six active contacts, impose progressively larger gaps, and optimize the remaining geometry at each continuation step. Reverse the continuation from several excursion depths. Archive feasible results by contact graph even when their scores initially decrease; release reflection symmetry before final refinement.

Escape through weighted-radius objective continuation. Optimize a sequence of objectives summing positive, nonuniform weights times radii, gradually increasing weight variation and then returning every weight to one. Use spatially correlated and reflection-compatible weight patterns, plus unrestricted patterns. Preserve distinct contact graphs encountered along each path and refine them under the original objective.

Search neighbouring circle counts as topology bridges. Produce diverse optimized 20-circle packings, insert a positive-radius circle into multiple distinct voids, and jointly refine all 21. Also optimize 22-circle packings and test deleting several different circles before refinement. Retain only canonical 21-circle outputs passing the frozen verifier, and archive distinct contact graphs rather than only immediate improvements.

Optimize a centered rectangle with variable width w and height 2-w, using squared pair-separation inequalities and linear wall constraints. The returned state is a 63-component vector containing all x coordinates, then all y coordinates, then all radii. A reflection-quotient stage shares coordinates and radii between mirrored circles.

Start local optimization from the highest-scoring verified feasible packing among the supplied incumbent, its repaired version, and a constructive baseline. Do not prioritize a supplied warm start merely because it exists; make it compete before allocating solver time.

When enforcing reflection symmetry through shared variables, retain all pairwise non-overlap and wall constraints on the expanded packing. Reduce the unknowns without also pruning symmetry-equivalent constraints; redundant constraint rows can change the numerical behavior of constrained local optimization.

Route search effort by incumbent quality: polish a strong warm start directly in the unrestricted model instead of spending the remaining budget imposing symmetry or perturbing it. Reserve symmetry-reduced construction for cold starts that still need a useful contact graph.

After constrained optimization, polish nearly active constraints with a few rank-revealing least-squares Newton corrections. Require full column rank and small correction steps, and retain candidates only after overlap repair, conservative perimeter normalization, and exact verifier-equivalent feasibility checks.

Express non-overlap constraints as Euclidean centre distance minus the sum of radii, rather than scaled squared-distance residuals. Supply analytic Jacobians, safeguarding division by near-zero distances. This keeps constraint residuals in length units and avoids radius-dependent scaling that can impair local optimization of unequal circles.

For low-quality starts, search several contact-rich staggered lattice families in a reflection-reduced space with three axis circles and nine mirrored pairs. Vary row populations to explore distinct packing basins, divide the seeding budget among them, then spend the remaining budget refining the best feasible candidate with symmetry unrestricted.

Express circle non-overlap as the distance gap ‖c_i−c_j‖−r_i−r_j ≥ 0 rather than a weighted squared-distance residual. Supply its analytic Jacobian to the constrained optimizer, flooring the distance denominator near zero. This keeps feasibility residuals in length units and avoids radius-dependent scaling of contact gradients.

Diversify by construction rather than only perturbing one local optimum: build several distinct triangular-lattice packing families directly as three axis circles plus nine reflected pairs, and allocate each a separate local-optimization budget. This preserves exact symmetry while exploring different starting contact structures without relying on projection from an asymmetric solution.

Express non-overlap constraints as Euclidean center distance minus the sum of radii, with analytic Jacobians, instead of weighted squared-distance residuals. This keeps residuals in geometric length units and avoids conditioning that depends on weights frozen from the initial radii; guard division by near-zero distances when forming derivatives.

Exploit reflection symmetry in both variables and constraints: optimize one representative per mirrored circle pair and one nonoverlap constraint per reflection orbit, removing duplicate wall constraints as well. Use the smaller problem for exploration, then release symmetry for a final full-dimensional polish.

Express nonoverlap as center distance minus the sum of radii, rather than a fixed-weight squared-distance residual. Supply analytic Jacobians, guarding division by near-zero distances. This keeps constraint residuals in length units and avoids scaling that becomes stale as radii change.

Search several reflection-symmetric packing families, varying both the number of axis circles and the allocation of mirrored pairs between rows. Archive the best nearly feasible solution from each family, then restart from promising entries with symmetry-preserving perturbations to centers and rectangle aspect ratio while initially leaving radii unchanged.

Express non-overlap as center distance minus the sum of radii, rather than a difference of squared quantities, and supply its analytic Jacobian. In symmetry-reduced models, remove algebraically duplicate pair and wall constraints before optimization to reduce redundant work and improve the local solver’s constraint scaling.

Run weighted-radius continuation with positive spatially correlated weights. Increase weight variation through several finite stages, then return weights gradually to one. Explore both reflection-compatible and unrestricted patterns. Archive distinct contact graphs along the path, including lower-scoring feasible states; refine each under the original objective and validate with the frozen verifier.

Use circle-count bridges: optimize diverse 20-circle configurations, locate several maximal empty disks inside each rectangle, insert a positive-radius twenty-first circle, and jointly optimize. Independently optimize 22-circle configurations and delete different circles before refinement. Submit only exactly 21 circles, and retain distinct contact graphs rather than only immediately improving bridge states.

For coordinated contact surgery, remove connected groups of three to six active contacts and compute nullspace directions of the remaining active-constraint Jacobian. Continue along both signs with constrained correction, allowing temporary objective loss until a new contact appears. Restart optimization from each event, archive distinct graphs, and independently verify final candidates.

Represent a packing by separate center and radius arrays, with optimization performed in a reflection quotient and an auxiliary rectangle-width coordinate. Before emission, repair overlaps by radius contraction and normalize the exact bounding perimeter. The adapter only reassembles the arrays; canonical warm starts remain accepted unchanged.

Reduce constraints as well as variables under reflection symmetry: retain one non-overlap constraint per reflected pair orbit, constrain mirrored representatives to one half-plane, and keep only nonredundant wall inequalities. This avoids feeding duplicate constraints to the local optimizer.

Precompute linear maps from optimization variables to coordinates, radius sums, and wall slacks. Evaluate analytic distance Jacobians through these maps, and cache constraint values and Jacobians at each iterate so separate solver callbacks reuse the same calculation.

Reduce both variables and constraints by reflection symmetry: share coordinates and radii across mirrored circles, retain one nonoverlap constraint per reflection orbit, and impose wall constraints only on representative circles. Assemble derivatives directly in reduced coordinates, accumulating contributions when a contact references the same reduced variable multiple times, including self-mirror contacts.

Escape through positive weighted-radius objectives. Apply spatially correlated weight patterns at several amplitudes, optimize each continuation stage, then gradually return weights to one. Test both reflection-compatible and unrestricted patterns. Preserve feasible states with distinct contact graphs despite temporary score loss; refine them under the original objective and check the frozen verifier.

Trace finite contact-release branches. Remove connected clusters of three to six active contacts, compute nullspace directions of the remaining active Jacobian, and follow both signs with constrained correction until a new contact appears. Permit temporary objective loss, archive distinct event graphs, and release reflection symmetry before final refinement.

Diversify reflection constructions across odd numbers of axis circles, not just three, and across different off-axis row populations. Enforce exactly 21 expanded circles. Allocate independent optimization slices to each family, retain distinct feasible contact graphs, and refine promising candidates without symmetry before exact verification.

Break accidental symmetry before the first local solve: retain horizontal reflection through three axis circles and nine mirrored pairs, but independently jitter each orbit’s horizontal coordinate and, more mildly, its vertical offset. This allows the symmetry-reduced optimizer to leave the initially left–right-symmetric layout without sacrificing the enforced reflection.

Run positive weighted-radius continuation using spatially correlated weights, with both reflection-compatible and unrestricted patterns. Increase weight variation until contacts change, then gradually restore unit weights. Archive feasible intermediate packings by contact graph even when their original scores decrease; refine distinct graphs under the original objective and validate using the frozen verifier.

Release connected groups of three to six active contacts, including mirrored groups when symmetry is enforced. Compute nullspace directions of the remaining active Jacobian and continue in both signs with constrained correction until a new contact appears. Permit temporary objective loss; archive event graphs and refine them after releasing symmetry.

Use neighbouring circle counts as topology bridges. Optimize diverse 20-circle packings, insert a positive-radius circle into several distinct empty regions, and jointly refine. Separately optimize 22-circle packings and delete different circles before refinement. Preserve distinct contact graphs, and submit only exactly 21 circles passing the frozen verifier.

members.hypothesis: baseline: the seed program as written
A compact reflection-symmetric SLSQP search followed by unrestricted refinement will produce substantially better cold-start packings than penalty descent within the two-second budget.
Replacing the final stiff penalty stages with an analytic-Jacobian constrained SQP polish will produce higher-scoring valid cold-start packings within the same time budget.
Replacing the last high-penalty stages with an analytic constrained polish will improve cold-start scores by at least 0.01 while preserving the incumbent whenever refinement fails.
Replacing the final stiff penalty stages with an analytic-Jacobian constrained polish will produce higher valid scores from cold starts within the same time budget.
Replacing penalty continuation with analytic-Jacobian constrained optimization from staggered lattice starts will produce cold-start packings with radius sum above 2.30 within the time budget.
Optimizing several structured mixed-radius packings with analytic constraint derivatives will produce valid cold-start scores above 2.30 within the time budget.
Replacing the fixed-centre LP finish with an analytic-Jacobian joint SLSQP polish will improve cold-start scores by allowing centres and radii to settle together after penalty continuation.
Optimizing a 20-circle rectangular grid with one interstitial circle using analytic constrained gradients will produce a valid sum of radii above 2.25 from both cold starts.
Optimizing a reflection-symmetric, variable-radius hexagonal family should raise both cold-start scores above 2.2 within the time budget.
Replacing penalty continuation with analytic-Jacobian constrained optimization from a staggered packing will produce cold-start scores above 2.25 within the time limit.
Replacing the penalty schedule with analytic-Jacobian constrained optimization and structured restarts will produce substantially better cold-start packings within the two-second budget.
A symmetry-preserving nonlinear search initialized from staggered 21-circle layouts will reliably improve the cold starts to dense packings with radius sum above 2.2.
Analytic-gradient optimization from two dense, geometrically distinct packings will raise both cold-start scores above 2.25 within the time budget.
Analytic-gradient optimization from compact triangular-lattice packings will raise the cold-start score above 2.2 within the two-second budget.
Replacing the last stiff penalty stages with analytic-Jacobian constrained polishing will improve the cold-start packing scores by allowing coordinated centre and radius adjustments near tangency.
Replacing penalty continuation with time-limited analytic-Jacobian SLSQP from staggered layouts will raise the cold-start score above 2.25 within two seconds.

Direct warm-start constrained refinement, followed by reflection-quotient restarts and unrestricted polishing, will improve the mean archive score by at least 0.0005 without sacrificing either valid incumbent.
Direct warm-start SQP followed by short, progressively stronger geometric restarts will improve the mean archive score by at least 0.001 without sacrificing either incumbent.
Prioritizing constrained refinement of the supplied packing before structured restarts will improve the mean archive-start score by at least 0.001 while preserving every verified incumbent.

Prioritizing warm-start polishing and short, progressively stronger perturbation restarts will improve the mean verified score of the two archived starts more than restarting exclusively from staggered lattices.
Analytic-gradient local optimization followed by localized multi-circle perturbations will improve the mean score of the two archive starts while preserving every already-valid incumbent.
Combining immediate warm-start refinement with a reflection-symmetric staggered restart and unrestricted final polishing will improve the mean score of the two archive starts by at least 0.001.
Prioritizing warm-start polishing and short contact-releasing restarts will improve the mean verified score of the two archived starts by at least 1e-5.
Successive separating-plane linear programs followed by analytic constrained polishing will improve the mean archive-start score by at least 0.0001 while preserving every valid incumbent.
Analytic-Jacobian constrained polishing followed by moderate topology-changing perturbations will improve the mean warm-start score by at least 0.001 while preserving every verified incumbent.
Warm-started SLSQP followed by short, incumbent-centred perturbation restarts will improve the mean neighbour score by at least 0.001 over searches that restart only from fixed lattice constructions.
Prioritizing warm-start SQP refinement and then alternating soft-penalty relaxation with constrained polishing will improve the mean score of the two archived starts by at least 0.0005.

Prioritizing warm-start polishing and then using short, progressively larger local restarts will improve the mean archive score by at least 0.0001 compared with spending the initial budget on unrelated grid packings.
Analytic-Jacobian joint optimization followed by several small topology-breaking perturbations will improve the mean score of the two archived starts while retaining every verified incumbent.
Replacing the full pairwise SLSQP constraint set with an adaptively expanded contact working set will permit more refinement steps within two seconds and improve the mean neighbor score.
Direct constrained refinement of each warm start, followed by a short penalty-assisted perturbation and a second constrained polish, will improve the mean archive score by at least 0.0001.

Initializing the existing reflection-symmetric SLSQP search from the nearest symmetric projection of the supplied packing will improve the mean neighbour score by at least 0.0001 compared with always restarting from the lattice.
High-accuracy contact-system polishing followed by reflection-symmetric coordinated restarts will recover at least 1e-10 of radius sum while preserving the verified incumbent.
Symmetry-preserving, coordinated three-pair perturbations followed by analytic constrained polishing can escape the incumbent contact graph and improve the verified radius sum by at least 1e-10.
Preserving the incumbent's radii and contact geometry during the first constrained refinement will recover at least 1e-10 of score if the incumbent retains numerical optimization slack.
Routing the unmodified warm start directly into high-accuracy SQP before penalty restarts will recover at least 1e-10 in radius sum if the incumbent retains numerical optimization slack.
Combining immediate warm-start polishing with contact-set refinement and alternating geometric restarts will improve the verified radius sum by at least 1e-10 while preserving the incumbent.
Reflection-preserving, coordinated perturbations of several circle orbits will reach a different contact topology and improve the incumbent radius sum by at least 1e-10.
Searching a reflection-orbit formulation with coordinated releases of three to five contacts will find a different packing basin and improve the verified radius sum by at least 1e-10.
Reflection-reduced optimization with coordinated three-contact releases will escape the incumbent contact topology and produce a verified gain of at least 1e-10.

Contact-equation polishing followed by reflection-preserving, multi-circle perturbations will improve the incumbent by at least 1e-10 if its remaining loss is numerical slack or a nearby symmetric contact rearrangement.
Combining exact constrained polishing with reflection-preserving, penalty-relaxed restarts will escape a coordinated-contact barrier and improve the incumbent radius sum by at least 1e-10.

Reducing the incumbent to its reflection quotient and using coordinated multi-circle restarts will permit more topology-changing optimization attempts and can improve the verified radius sum by at least 1e-10.

Warm-started contact-set SQP followed by active-contact Newton polishing will improve the incumbent by at least 1e-10, while short coordinated perturbations provide additional chances to change its contact graph.

Structured symmetric starts followed by short basin probes and incumbent-focused polishing will outperform symmetry projection of the tiny cold-start circles, reaching a verified radius sum above 2.30.

Using reflection symmetry only for initialization, followed by unrestricted Cartesian polishing, will preserve strong cold-start solutions while improving packings trapped by the fixed orbit representation.

A coarse-to-fine portfolio of symmetric lattice starts will produce better cold-start packings than projecting the tiny initial circles into a single orbit configuration.
Optimizing several distinct reflection-symmetric row families with analytic constraint derivatives will improve cold-start radius sums from 0.021 to above 2.3.
Analytic-gradient multistart optimization of twelve reflection orbits will turn both cold starts into valid packings with radius sum above 2.30.
Replacing projection of poor cold starts with a staged search over triangular and staggered reflection-symmetric seeds will improve the mean verified cold-start score by at least 0.05.

Replacing cold-start projection with several structured reflection-symmetric seeds and staged SLSQP polishing will improve the mean cold-start score by finding a better packing basin within the same budget.

Replacing sequential full-length solves with a short screening round followed by ranked polishing will improve the mean verified score by giving promising structured starts time to converge before the deadline.
